texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an envoy of {FACTION}, has come about {DEAD}. {FACTION} know {A_nameDef} has sworn on them for it, and they would rather pay than bleed: {COUNT} silver, the old blood price, laid down for {DEAD}'s life, and the matter closed for good.\n\n{A_nameDef} has heard. {A_pronoun} hasn't said anything yet.

[atwar] An envoy of {FACTION} is waiting at the edge of the colony's land under a white cloth. {FACTION} are still at war with the colony, but they want this one thing settled: they offer {COUNT} silver as the blood price for {DEAD}, if {A_nameDef} will lay down {A_possessive} oath.

[taken] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come about {DEAD}, who {FACTION} carried off. They can't give {DEAD} back, {X_pronoun} says, and won't pretend otherwise. But they will pay {COUNT} silver as the price of what they did, if {A_nameDef} will let the matter rest.

[heir] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come about {DEAD}, and about the oath {A_nameDef} took up when the one who swore it died. {FACTION} offer {COUNT} silver, the blood price, to end it before it outlives anyone else.

[pet] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come, a little awkwardly, about {DEAD}, {A_nameDef}'s animal. {FACTION} have heard {A_nameDef} swore on them for it, and would rather pay {COUNT} silver than find out how seriously.

li.label: Take the blood price
li.outcome: The silver is counted out on a blanket, and {A_nameDef} stands over it a long time before saying the words that end it. {X_nameDef} bows, and goes.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} decide
li.outcome: The council leaves it to {A_nameDef}: it was {A_possessive} oath. {A_nameDef} goes out to hear {X_nameDef} alone.

li.label: Some things aren't for sale
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is told the colony doesn't sell its dead. {X_pronoun} takes the silver home, and {FACTION} will have to live with {A_nameDef}'s oath.

outcomes.li: [taken] {X_nameDef} is told the colony wants {DEAD} back, not silver. {X_pronoun} has no answer to that, and goes home with the purse.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}, has come to the colony now that there's peace, and asked to speak to {A_nameDef}. {X_pronoun} has come to say what {FACTION} never said while they were at war: that they are sorry for {DEAD}. Not for the war. For {DEAD}.\n\n{X_pronoun} doesn't ask {A_nameDef} to forgive anything. {X_pronoun} only asks to be heard.

[taken] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to say it plainly to {A_nameDef}: carrying off {DEAD} was wrong, and {FACTION} are sorry for it. {X_pronoun} doesn't know where {DEAD} is now. {X_pronoun} wishes {X_pronoun} did.

[heir] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to {A_nameDef}, who took up the oath for {DEAD} when its first keeper died. {FACTION} are sorry, {X_pronoun} says, for {DEAD} and for everything that came after.

[pet] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to say sorry about {DEAD}. It was only an animal, some among {FACTION} say. {X_nameDef} has come anyway, because {X_pronoun} heard what {DEAD} was to {A_nameDef}.

li.label: {A_nameDef} hears them, and accepts
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} sit together for an hour. When they stand, {A_nameDef} says it's over, and {X_nameDef} weeps, which nobody expected.

li.label: Let them say it in front of everyone
li.outcome: The colony gathers, and {X_nameDef} says it in front of all of them: {FACTION} are sorry for {DEAD}. Then everyone looks at {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Sorry changes nothing
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} is told that {DEAD} is still gone, and that sorry doesn't change it. {X_pronoun} nods as if {X_pronoun} expected nothing else, and goes.
